newsitem.title: UK: Holidays hit quiet freight market, trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Holidays hit quiet freight market, trend unclear.

text.p: Caper business was more or less at a standstill and the rest of the dry cargo freight market was just ticking over, brokers reported on Monday.
Christmas and New Year breaks combined with holidays almost throughout this week in Japan and South Korea reduced fixture turnover drastically and will continue to do so, they said.

Market trends were inevitably more difficult to evaluate but some observers believed Far East panamax rates continued to ease a little, although few early panamaxes were said to be available in any principal loading areas. The BFI was down 1 at 1,516.

Grain - Continental was understood to have fixed two or three panamaxes for grain in the Atlantic. The only one adequately reported was the 20-year old Ermioni, 66,157 dwt, delivery spot Mobile trip Skaw-Passero at $9,000 daily plus $175,000 bonus. Bluedeck was linked with Apollonia Lion 72,044 dwt open prompt Continent for grain from US Gulf to Egypt but further details were lacking.

Cargill quoted a fresh panamax grain enquiry of 2.9/3m cft grain Mississippi/Gibraltar-Hamburg range option Spanish Med or UK for Jan 13/20, ideas $13.00 basis 49'. Otherwise the grain market was almost devoid of new business.

In the handy sector there were rumours of about 27,000 tonnes heavy grain fixed US Gulf/Portugal for mid-Jan at $18.00/18.50, and Grain Coop booked Grigorpan for 25,000 grains 53' up river/Lisbon for early Jan at a steady $23.50.

Minerals - Seyang was reported to have agreed a hefty $14,250 daily plus $305,000 bonus for the 1984-built Dimitris Perottis 64,933 dwt delivery US Gulf mid-Jan for a trip Far East. Brokers speculated that this vessel was not suitable for grain and that therefore the fixture might be to cover fertilizers to China.

A fixture by Cosco Singapore of Maersk Taikung 70,400 dwt delivery prompt Bremen for a trip via US Gulf to China at $15,500 daily was believed to have failed on subjects. Full information continued to be unavailable on rumoured short period fixtures in the Atlantic by Deiulemar of Umberto D'amato 75,000 dwt and by Cobelfret of Orjen 72,150 dwt.

Handysizes - Brokers reported difficulties fixing early tonnage in the Far East. The North Atlantic was also proving awkward for certain types in prompt positions although a modern 40,000 dwt vessel was rumoured taken from the continent or Baltic to the US Gulf close to a steady $7,750 daily.
